assumptions: Finite complex Hilbert chain with bounded differentials, adjacent zero compositions and reduced exactness; only S1 assumes finite-dimensional original layers.
quantifiers: Every degree of every finite chain, all original vectors, including zero-dimensional layers and both endpoint maps. The proof also works for r=0, so in particular every task r>=1.
domains: H(n+1) is task H_n, d(n) is task d_(n-1), H(0) and H(r+2) are literal zero endpoint spaces expressed by Subsingleton. No hypothesis is imposed on the unused tail. Reduced exactness is exactly closure(range d(n))=ker d(n+1).
conclusions: Finite-dimensional domains give closed ranges. The actual restricted map d:ker(d)-orthogonal -> range(d) is bijective and has a continuous inverse. The constructed s and G have both endpoint zeros, every contraction equation, and both inverse equations. Norm s is at most the restricted inverse norm; norm G is at most C_j squared, where C_j=max(1,the two adjacent restricted inverse norms). The true energy lower bound C_j^-2 is proved.
representation: Closed reduced exactness identifies range(d) with the next kernel, so the reducedEquiv codomain is exactly the task Z at the next degree. Complex energy inequalities use the real part; the Laplacian is proved self-adjoint and its energy equals the real nonnegative squared-norm sum. No finite-length/finite-dimension substitution.

assumptions: Arbitrary complex Hilbert layers, original positive energy constants lambda_j, actual differential norm errors bounded by delta_j and eta_j<lambda_j. The new differential chain identity is explicitly required for the new contraction, and the original identity for the original contraction.
quantifiers: Every admissible pair of differential chains, each degree and every original vector. The specified endpoint delta=0 is a permitted instance of the slightly stronger estimates allowing any nonnegative valid upper bound.
domains: L and L-prime are the actual adjoint-product Laplacians. perturbationEta is precisely 2norm(dprev)deltaPrev+deltaPrev^2+2norm(dnext)deltaNext+deltaNext^2. c in Lean denotes task lambda; no scalar-ordering on complex numbers is introduced.
conclusions: The actual Laplacian difference is bounded by eta, the perturbed energy is bounded below by lambda-eta, and both Green operators are actual continuous inverses. The bound norm G-prime <= 1/(lambda-eta), the specified inverse difference bound eta/[lambda(lambda-eta)], and the s-prime-s bound deltaPrev/(lambda-eta)+norm(dprev)eta/[lambda(lambda-eta)] all hold. The actual adjoint-times-inverse formula yields the new contraction at every finite degree and zero endpoints.
representation: finiteGreen is constructed from a coercive continuous linear equivalence at each relevant degree; its zero extension only occupies unused indices. All inverse and chain identities are proved, not stored as certificate fields. Adjacent shifted and unshifted intertwining is derived from the actual chain equations. No finite-dimensional assumption is carried from S1.

assumptions: Only the task common finite complex Hilbert chain hypotheses and reduced exactness. No closed range, finite dimension or positive spectral gap.
quantifiers: A genuine length-one example refutes the claimed universal construction, at both of its original degrees.
domains: Actual lp(N,Complex,2), with zero-based n representing positive task index n+1. The differential has exact coefficient 1/(n+1), bounded norm one, and both zero endpoint maps.
conclusions: The differential is injective and has dense range, so both reduced records vanish. No bounded left inverse, bounded right inverse or chain contraction exists. The true two Laplacians are the diagonal with coefficient 1/(n+1)^2, both injective and neither admits a bounded linear right inverse. Its range is not closed.
representation: Finite coordinate vectors lie in the actual range and their norm-convergent expansion proves density. The inverse obstruction is proved on actual unit vectors in l2, without a finite-dimensional proxy. The complex field and both endpoint requirements are retained.

assumptions: Exactly reduced exactness from S3 and positive real epsilon for inverse identities. No closed range or quantitative lower bound is assumed for the original Laplacian.
quantifiers: Every epsilon>0, every finite-chain degree and every original vector; one-sided epsilon tending to zero. The failure of operator norm convergence is witnessed at both degrees of the S3 example.
domains: regularGreen is the actual inverse of L+epsilon I built by coercivity. For a convenient total function it is assigned zero only when epsilon<=0; all inverse statements use epsilon>0 and all limits use the punctured right-neighborhood filter. The vector spaces and linear maps are genuinely complex.
conclusions: Regular inverse exists with norm<=1/epsilon. The finite contraction sum equals I-epsilon G_epsilon including endpoints. The real Laplacian energy and reduced exactness imply injectivity, self-adjointness implies dense range, and uniform boundedness extends the proved range convergence to every vector. The same S3 diagonal has no operator norm convergence of I-epsilon G to I.
representation: The complex density argument is explicitly proved; the real-only GR105 helper is not claimed as a complex theorem. The norm counterexample follows alternatively from a proved Neumann-series implication: norm epsilon G ->0 would give a bounded right inverse, contradicting S3. This is independent of the finite-chain four-way theorem and avoids circular use of S5.

assumptions: Exactly the original finite complex chain and reduced exactness. Closed ranges, contraction, right inverses and regularization norm limits are the four properties being compared, not additional common assumptions.
quantifiers: All four conditions, every implication, every finite degree including endpoints and all original vectors. Every bounded right inverse is proved to be a two-sided inverse in this setting.
domains: The closure and exact range remain distinct in the formulas. The final criterion is finite and imposes no tail assumptions. The regularization condition is the operator norm of epsilon times the actual shifted inverse.
conclusions: All ranges closed iff a bounded chain contraction exists iff every Laplacian has a bounded right inverse iff every epsilon-resolvent norm tends to zero. A small error operator has a proved convergent Neumann inverse; conversely an actual right inverse gives an explicit O(epsilon) error norm bound. Under the equivalent properties, the actual s=dprev-adjoint G has the full contraction equations, zero endpoints and norm <= norm(dprev)norm(G). Restricted-inverse bounds and finite uniform Lipschitz constants are provided.
representation: The Green operators are constructed, not supplied as a proof certificate. Uniform constants are finite sums of actual operator norms over exactly the finite range; this supplies the requested finite bounds without assuming a uniform estimate on an unused infinite tail. Zero-dimensional Hilbert layers are allowed throughout.
